Formulation
- Predisposing: History of IBS; no prior urinary tract infections reported

No systemic features (fever, loin pain) reported. Past history notable for IBS and allergy to clindamycin. Patient agreed to an empirical short course of antibiotics and was advised on supportive measures and safety signs requiring re-evaluation.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Suspected acute lower urinary tract infection (dysuria, hematuria, suprapubic pain)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Resolution of urinary symptoms (pain, blood in urine, odor)
  - Avoid complications (upper urinary tract involvement, retention)
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Treat suspected UTI promptly with appropriate antibiotic therapy
  - Monitor for signs of systemic infection or complications and arrange review if needed
- Actions (Patient):
  - Obtain and commence prescribed antibiotic as soon as available (prescription sent to requested pharmacy)
  - Increase oral fluid intake (advised 2.5–3.0 liters/day)
  - Consider cranberry juice and urine pH/acidifying sachets as advised
  - Acquire a thermometer and check for fever at home
  - Seek urgent review if developing high temperature/fever, worsening pain, new loin/back pain, inability to pass urine, or if symptoms do not improve
  - Pick up prescribed medication from Knightsbridge pharmacy as requested (pharmacy name recorded)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Prescription for an antibiotic was issued and sent to the patient’s requested pharmacy (antibiotic name/dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript)
  - Advised increased fluids, cranberry, and urine acidity sachets as adjunctive measures
  - Advised patient to monitor temperature and return if systemic features, worsening pain, urinary retention, or recurrent infections
  - Document allergy to clindamycin in record
  - Offer further evaluation if infections recur (arrange follow-up/investigations if recurrent)

Secondary Problem: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Not recorded
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Not recorded
- Actions (Patient):
  - Continue current medication Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily (patient-reported regimen)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Likely diagnosis (urinary tract infection)
  - Antibiotic treatment recommended (three-day course discussed; exact regimen not documented)
  - Importance of fluid intake (2.5–3 L/day)
  - Adjunct measures: cranberry juice, urine-acidity sachets available OTC
  - Warning signs requiring re-evaluation: high temperature/fever, worsening pain, loin/back pain, inability to pass urine, lack of improvement or recurrent episodes
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - New or rising temperature/fever
  - New or worsening loin/back pain
  - Inability to pass urine
  - Increasing abdominal pain or persistent hematuria
  - Recurrent urinary symptoms after treatment
- Coping Strategies:
  - Maintain hydration
  - Use community pharmacy products as advised (cranberry, urine pH sachets)
  - Seek prompt medical review if warning signs develop
